rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The project (sc.result inside person.se_line2, has_sc gate) and the candidate (sum of sc.line31) give the same Schedule SE line 13 (Step 2 copies it); sc.result equals sc.line31 except that a loss with some investment not at risk is refused at sc.loss_allowed (i1040sc p. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. The deepseek-flash line rebuilds Schedule SE from helpers (line 4c, line 10 on the smaller of line 6 or the wage base less wages, line 11, half of line 12) and agrees with the project's se definition wherever both evaluate. In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi EIC Worksheet B, Part 1 and Part 2 (Schedule SE line 3 less line 13 if you file Schedule SE, otherwise Schedule C line 31), with i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The candidate always takes line 3 less line 13; below the $400 threshold line 13 is zero and line 3 is the Schedule C total, so the value equals the project's choice. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. For a SEP the candidate deducts Step 21, the maximum deductible contribution, whatever was contributed; the project deducts person.sep_contrib and refuses a contribution above Step 21 (person.sep_excess). A SEP contribution below the maximum is over-deducted: a sole proprietor with $50,000 of Schedule C profit, a 10% plan and a $2,000 contribution deducts about $4,200 (Step 21) in the candidate and $2,000 in the project (derived from the expressions, not executed). The SIMPLE branch (deferral plus employer contributions) is the project's, which refuses amounts above the limits (person.simple_excess); the candidate also lacks the Schedule C gate (i1040gi p. 93, Line 16, "If you were self-employed or a partner") and refuses plan_screen for everyone (placement).

Ruling: model error; p560 p. 16, Employer matching contributions: "You are generally required to match each employee's salary reduction contribution(s) on a dollar-for-dollar basis up to 3% of the employee's compensation", and catch-up contributions are limited to the excess of compensation over regular contributions. The candidate caps the SIMPLE total (deferral plus employer contribution) only at Schedule SE line 4c, so an employer contribution above 3% or 2% of compensation, or catch-up contributions above their limits, are deducted rather than limited or refused; its SEP branch uses Step 21 built on its Step 5, ruled model error. The returns that would show it are unevaluable in this graph (stage14.simple.refuse_employer, stage14.simple.refuse_catchup, stage14.simple.refuse_catchup_comp, stage14.sep.refuse_excess: project refuses at person.simple_excess or person.sep_excess, candidate cycle at sc_total), so this is ruled on the derivation. rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The project (sc.result inside person.se_line2, has_sc gate) and the candidate (sum of sc.line31) give the same line; sc.result equals sc.line31 except that a loss with some investment not at risk is refused at sc.loss_allowed (i1040sc p. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The project (sc.result inside person.se_line2, has_sc gate) and the candidate (sum of sc.line31) give the same line; sc.result equals sc.line31 except that a loss with some investment not at risk is refused at sc.loss_allowed (i1040sc p. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. The deepseek-flash line rebuilds Schedule SE from helpers (line 4c, line 10 on the smaller of line 6 or the wage base less wages, line 11, half of line 12) and agrees with the project's se definition wherever both evaluate. In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.deepseek.json): 2,317 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 220 candidate-refuses, 2103 candidate-unknown, 7 project-refuses.
